harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restored branch_ledger using RHEL-supported MariaDB 10.11.18. Node1 is the application writer; node2 is a read-only replica. Replication, disconnect catch-up, application write denial, exact data preservation, and persistence across both node reboots all passed.
actions_performed: Restored original IDs 1001/1002 and amounts 12.50/-3.25; preserved the staged SQL export unchanged.
Configured durable row-based binary logging on node1 and crash-recoverable, read-only replication on node2.
Created a node-generated ledger_repl account restricted to REPLICATION SLAVE and node2's IP.
Created ledger_app with only SELECT/INSERT privileges; its credential is stored at /root/.branch-ledger-app.cnf with mode 0600.
Verified normal replication, bounded disconnect catch-up, no missing or duplicate IDs, and replica write rejection.
Restarted node2 and node1 sequentially, proving changed boot identities and complete recovery after each.
Left SELinux enforcing, firewalld active with peer-specific rules, no failed units, and no temporary credential-transfer residue.

evidence.requirement: Restore the staged ledger while retaining IDs, amounts, and export
evidence.summary: Original and final export hashes match; final data includes the original exact rows and all committed test rows.

evidence.requirement: Use platform-compatible database software without changing OS/kernel
evidence.summary: MariaDB 10.11.18 came from RHEL AppStream; RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained installed.
ledger_repl has only REPLICATION SLAVE, and node2 actively uses it with healthy I/O and SQL threads.

evidence.requirement: Committed inserts on node1 arrive on node2
evidence.summary: Application inserts 1003 and post-restart 1006 appeared automatically on node2 with identical values.

evidence.requirement: Node1 remains the sole application writer
evidence.summary: The same ledger_app identity writes on node1 but receives read-only error 1290 on node2; unauthorized row counts remained zero.

evidence.requirement: Catch up after a short disconnect without loss or duplication
evidence.summary: Node2 stopped at three rows/position 2008, node1 committed two rows, then node2 caught up to position 2441 with 5 rows, 5 distinct IDs, exact values, zero lag, and no errors.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node2 restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, and fully recovered read-only replication/data are directly shown.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, recovered writer/data, and node2's automatic reconnection are directly shown.

evidence.requirement: Final health, security, cleanup, and exact data state
evidence.summary: Both nodes are healthy with exact six-row data, six distinct IDs, total 34.75, unchanged exports, active security controls, restricted listeners, no temporary residue, and no failed units.
